context_for_next_testing_agent: Critical fix applied: auth_utils.py now uses user['id'] = str(user.pop('_id')) instead of user['_id'] = str(user['_id']). This fixed 500 errors on all operator/device creation endpoints. Backend 15/15 passing. Frontend fully functional. Remaining issues: no brute force protection, dead code in change_password. Speed test is MOCKED (by design). AI tab hidden when ai_enabled=False (by design).

rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: In auth_utils.py get_current_user(), the MongoDB document's '_id' was converted to string but kept as key '_id'. When any endpoint called current_user['id'], it raised KeyError because the key was '_id' not 'id'. This affected operators.py (create_operator), devices.py (create_device), users.py (create_user) and any other endpoint accessing current_user['id'].
rca_of_the_issue.fix: Changed `user['_id'] = str(user['_id'])` to `user['id'] = str(user.pop('_id'))` which properly renames the key from '_id' to 'id'.
rca_of_the_issue.reproduction: POST /api/operators with valid auth would return 500 Internal Server Error
